doc.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Double bass drums and the great drummers
title: Engineering the hi-hat to work alongside two bass drums
summary: He removed the hi-hat tripod and linked it to the bass drum rod, working out a toe-and-heel technique.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: How did you negotiate working a bass drum and the pedal with your left foot? I mean the sock cymbal – the hi-hat cymbal.

I took the tripod off of the hi-hat and made a connection between the bell of the hi-hat and one of the rods in the bass drum, so that brought it right – this was the bass drum, and the hi-hat was right next to it, by getting rid of the tripod.
So you had to be an engineering designer as well.
Yeah. In those days I was playing toe with the bass drum and heel with the hi- hat, or both together.
So you had to come up with your own technique and approach.
